title: Sign Restrictions and Supply-demand Decompositions of Inflation
hypothesis: Supply-demand sign restrictions (upward supply, downward demand) sharply identify historical decompositions of US inflation (aggregate and disaggregated). Paper shows they generally yield wide identified sets largely uninformative, unlike impulses/elasticities/FEVDs where rho alone governs identification, because historical decomposition informativeness depends on both rho and realized forecast errors.
data_sources: GP24 replication code/data 1997:Q1-2019:Q4 log CPI + log real GDP (US) and HICP (euro area) quarterly; Minnesota + sum-of-coefficients prior following Giannone-Lenza-Primiceri 2015.
BEA National Accounts Underlying Detail Tables monthly PCE prices and real expenditures per category; construction monthly PCE inflation ~ log differences, year-ended = sum_{l=0}^{11} monthly.
sample: Aggregate: four-lag Bayesian VAR in log CPI and log real GDP estimated 1997:Q1--2019:Q4 with Minnesota + sum-of-coefficients prior (Giannone-Lenza-Primiceri 2015); historical decomposition of post-2019 forecast errors in year-ended CPI inflation (p_t - p_{t-4}, quarterly data) given info up to 2019:Q4; euro area analogous with HICP. Disaggregated: 12-lag OLS VAR in monthly PCE inflation (log differences) and real expenditure growth per category 1988:M1--2023:M9, 136 PCE categories; transformation to year-ended inflation 12-month sum; object H_{1,t} sum_{h=0}^{11} contribution to monthly then year-ended; categories with explosive VAR noted. Three-variable illustrative DGP: 100 one-step forecast errors with rho12≈-1, small rho13 positive, rho23 negative, used to show set includes zero and u_pt.
method: 1. Define SVAR(p) y_t=(p_t,q_t)' = B x_t + Sigma_tr Q eps_t; B = A0^{-1}A+, Sigma= A0^{-1}A0^{-1}', Q in O(2) parametrized by theta in [-pi,pi] via rotation matrix; reduced-form phi = (vec(B)', vech(Sigma_tr)')' ; innovation correlation rho = sigma21 / sqrt(sigma21^2+sigma22^2).

2. Impose sign restrictions A0^{-1} = [[+,+],[-,+]] (supply: p and q opposite; demand: same) equivalently A0=[[+,-],[+,+]] upward supply, downward demand; induces identified set IS_theta(phi) = [arctan(sigma22/sigma21),0] if rho<0 else [-pi/2, arctan(-sigma21/sigma22)] and IS_omega^s, IS_omega^d as in text.

3. Historical decomposition for supply shock: H_{t,t+h}(theta,phi,{u})= [cos theta sin theta] Omega_h(phi,{u}) [cos theta; sin theta] where Omega_h = sum_{l=0}^h c_{1l}(phi)(Sigma_tr^{-1} u_{t+h-l})' with c_{1h}'= e1' C_h Sigma_tr via recursion C_h = sum_{l=1}^{min(h,p)} B_l C_{h-l}, C0=I2. Focus object H_{t,t+h}=H_{1,1,t,t+h} but extends to transformed year-ended: for quarterly pi^{(ye)}_t = p_t - p_{t-4}, H = H_{t,t+h} h=0..3 and H_{t,t+h}-H_{t,t+h-4} h>=4 => replace Omega with tilde Omega_h = Omega_h - Omega_{h-4} (eq D.2); monthly to year-ended 12-month sum tilde Omega_{t-1}= sum_{h=0}^{11} Omega_{t-h}.

4. Identified set IS_H = {H(theta): theta in IS_theta} = [L,U] continuous in theta. Numerically compute bounds: candidate values at two endpoints of IS_theta plus up to two eigenvectors of S_h=(Omega+Omega')/2 satisfying q1'q1=1 and sign normalization e1'A0 e1 >=0 ; check admissibility via atan2; L/U = min/max over admissible endpoints+critical points (no simulation error). Analytical special case h=0: H_{t,t}= u_pt cos^2 theta + C sin theta cos theta with C=(sigma11 u_qt - sigma21 u_pt)/sigma22; Proposition 1 gives theta^* = 0.5 arctan(R) or -pi/2 adjustment; Theta = {theta_bar,theta_under} U {theta^* if interior}; compare values at rho<0: rho^2 sigma11/sigma21 u_qt and u_pt; rho>=0: 0 and (1-rho^2)(u_pt - sigma21/sigma22 C).

5. Aggregate estimation: replicate GP24 exact reduced-form VAR 4 lags log CPI + log real GDP 1997:Q1-2019:Q4 Minnesota+sum-of-coefficients prior. Standard Bayes: draw phi posterior 10,000 draws, at each phi draw 10 draws theta uniform over IS_theta => 100,000 (phi,theta) compute posterior mean of year-ended decomposition. Prior-robust Bayes Giacomini-Kitagawa 2021: class of conditional priors assigning prob1 to IS_theta; set of posterior means approximated by posterior means of interval endpoints L/U at each phi draw; 1-tau robust credible interval approximated by [tau/2 quantile of L , 1-tau/2 quantile of U] with tau=0.32 (68% level); compute for each horizon t. Euro area same replacing CPI with HICP. Three-variable SVARs from GP24: replace inflation with energy/non-energy prices (demand+, non-energy supply -, energy supply moves energy vs GDP) or add interest rate (demand moves y,p,i +; supply y vs p; monetary i vs y,p for 4 periods sign of i response); approximate L/U via 10,000 Q draws uniform over identified set via Rubio-Ramirez-Waggoner-Zha accept-reject (K=10,494 ensures epsilon=delta=0.01 for d=17).

6. Disaggregated estimation: per category k OLS 12-lag VAR monthly PCE inflation (log diff) and real expenditure growth 1988:M1-2023:M9; compute u_t, rho; compute identified sets for H_{1,t} summed to year-ended via step 4 numeric procedure replacing Omega with tilde Omega_{t-1}; report inflation deviations from deterministic component (constant+initial conditions). Flag 2 explosive first-difference VARs. Report share vague stats about |rho| thresholds. Example categories min |rho| lubricants and fluids (<0.0001) and max -0.98 food produced/consumed on farms; illustrate March 2022 values.

7. Three-variable beyond-bivariate illustration: 3-var SVAR y=(p,q,z)', eps=(s,d,z)' sign restrictions on A0^{-1} and A0 as in text with ? unrestricted; DGP rho12≈-1 rho13 small positive rho23 small negative; simulate 100 forecast errors; approximate IS_H via ~55,000 Q draws ensuring misclassification ≤1% with prob ≥99% to show set includes 0 and u_pt despite strong rho.

8. Joint inference: hypothesis H = demand contribution > supply each quarter 2021:Q2-2022:Q2 equivalently tilde H_t ≤ 0.5 FE_t for t in T (5 quarters, 17 total post-2019 quarters). Compute posterior lower/upper probabilities via robust Bayes (Giacomini-Kitagawa-Read 2022 rejoinder) using 10,000 theta draws per phi; compare to uniform prior posterior ~0.5, lower 0, upper 0.99.
